sourceChecks.claim: MySQL overview defines relational SQL server with client programs and libraries; separate server execution and shared client access support the architecture described.
InnoDB introduction identifies default engine, ACID transactions/recovery, row-level locks and foreign keys; guarantees are correctly limited to its tables.

SQL-modes page explicitly demonstrates abc-to-INT warning/0 versus strict error. CHECK followup specifies TRUE/UNKNOWN acceptance and FALSE rejection, validating NOT NULL combination and enforcement caution. Types/keys/references are standard declared schema semantics, not workflow coordination.

COMMIT manual says default autocommit wraps standalone statements and START TRANSACTION groups until commit/rollback. InnoDB parameter followup confirms default redo flush-at-commit and crash-loss risk when relaxed; external HTTP is outside database rollback scope.

Isolation manual confirms default Repeatable Read first consistent-read snapshot and distinct locking/range behavior. Locking Reads confirms current-data exclusive locks; Deadlocks confirms default victim rollback and need to retry transactions.

Clustered/Secondary Indexes explicitly says secondary records contain PK columns and long PKs enlarge them; clustered lookup reaches row data. Workload-measured EXPLAIN/scan tradeoffs are consistent with linked optimization guidance.

Replication manual says default asynchronous source-to-replica copying; implementation followup says binary events enter relay log before processing. Therefore receipt is not application and unavailable unreplicated writes can be lost; promotion requires separate authority/routing design.

PITR manual requires restoring a base full backup then incremental later changes; binary-log followup describes applying logged updates. Gaps prevent desired reconstruction and replica propagation includes deletes; tests are evidence of recovery rather than the mere presence of files.

InnoDB introduction supplies the relational transactional capability basis; other cards establish index maintenance, lag, concurrency and recovery costs. Final selection appropriately remains conditional on measured workload and failure requirements.
